observation.visible_scene: A near-black night sky dominated by a thin vertical wire/strand holding three warm orange glowing bulbs, spaced top, middle and bottom near the left-center of the frame; each bright bulb casts a long diagonal lens-flare streak. The whole frame is peppered with many small bright specks and short motion-blur streaks (falling/drifting particles), and two faint green dots sit persistently on the right side.
visible_changes: The small bright particles are the main moving element: short diagonal streaks continuously cross the frame, with individual streaks appearing, shifting and vanishing from one sample to the next (already in motion at the first frame and still in motion at the last).

The strand of bulbs stays essentially in place but drifts/sways only slightly over the excerpt (top bulb moves a few pixels leftward between the first and last frames); the three bulbs and the wire keep the same vertical arrangement throughout.
The diagonal lens flares remain locked to their bulbs, translating with the bulbs rather than moving independently.
The two faint green points on the right stay at roughly fixed positions, showing no clear independent motion.
No editing cut is visible; the change between samples is continuous particle motion plus a very slight shift of the lit strand.
outside_clip_unknowns: The identity of the falling particles (snow, dust, embers, etc.) is not determinable from the frames.
What the wire/strand is attached to and whether its slight shift is wind sway or camera movement is unknown.
The cause of the lens flares (camera optics vs. scene geometry) and any events before or after this cropped segment are unseen.
uncertain_details: Exact direction and speed of the particle drift: streaks are diagonal but a single consistent vector cannot be confidently tracked.
Whether the few-pixel leftward shift of the bulbs is strand motion or camera pan; background is too sparse to disambiguate.
Whether the green dots are separate distant lights or reflections/artifacts.
